You are integrating Neatlogs observability into a typescript project.

## Detected Stack
- Language: typescript
- Package manager: pnpm
- Agent framework: langchain
- Web framework: nextjs
- LLM providers: openai
- TypeScript instrumentation is EXPLICIT and per-instance. Do not pass `init({ instrumentations: [...] })`: global instrumentors cannot guarantee isolation, and the remaining keys do not provide complete capture.
- Use these helpers for the detected libraries: langchainHandler() from 'neatlogs/langchain' via { callbacks: [handler] }; langchainHandler() from 'neatlogs/langchain', attached at the GRAPH invocation; wrapOpenAI() from 'neatlogs/openai'. Wrap/attach at the construction site (`const client = wrapOpenAI(new OpenAI())`) — plain static imports are fine, there is no import-order rule.
- This project is ALREADY instrumented with Neatlogs (neatlogs.init() exists in source). This is a RE-RUN.
  Do NOT re-add or duplicate neatlogs.init(), .env keys, wrap()/handler/processor setup, or existing @neatlogs.span decorators.
  Do NOT modify existing instrumentation. ONLY add instrumentation for NEW, currently-uninstrumented functions/agents. If everything is already instrumented, make no changes.

## Credentials
- Environment variable name: NEATLOGS_API_KEY
The secret value is held by the wizard and is intentionally absent from this prompt. Call configure_neatlogs_api_key with no arguments; never ask for, read, print, or echo the value.
Do NOT set an endpoint anywhere — no endpoint=/endpoint: in init(), no NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT in .env. Preserve an existing explicit self-hosted endpoint.

## Required init() pattern
neatlogs.init() MUST include api_key=os.getenv("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"). This is non-negotiable.
The SDK does NOT reliably read from env in all deployment scenarios (Docker, systemd, cron).

## Instrumentation anchors (from static analysis — start HERE, do not scan the whole repo)
The analyzer scanned 22 functions and found the 1 that anchor tracing. Instrument these and follow their connections (the tools / retrievers / chains each agent or route uses) by reading those functions. Skip everything else unless an anchor leads you to it.

## What deserves a WORKFLOW (and what does NOT)
A WORKFLOW span is the trace ROOT of a meaningful unit of AI work. Root ONLY entry points that (directly or transitively) reach an LLM/agent/tool/retriever — a chat / generate / analyze / agent-run / model-calling consumer. Do NOT root pure CRUD/read endpoints (list_*/get_*/create_*/update_*/delete_*, health/ping) — they just hit a DB and rooting them spams the platform with empty content-free traces that bury the real agent traces. Test: "if this ran, would its trace contain an LLM/tool/retriever span?" No → not a workflow, instrument nothing.
AUTO-ROOT (important): the provider wrappers (`neatlogs.wrap(client)` in Python, `wrapOpenAI`/`wrapAnthropic`/`wrapGoogleGenAI`/… in TypeScript) and Python `instrumentations=[...]` now open a WORKFLOW root AUTOMATICALLY when a provider/LLM call would otherwise be parentless — so a lone wrapped call does NOT orphan and renders on its own. You therefore add a manual `@span(kind="WORKFLOW")` at a feature entry point to GROUP a multi-step feature (several LLM calls + tools + your own functions) under ONE named root, NOT merely to make a single call render. If a manual root is active, the auto-root detects it and steps aside (never a double root). Framework handlers/processors (LangChain, OpenAI Agents, CrewAI) root themselves the same way.

## How to work: FIRST TRACE FAST, then fan out, then verify
Your FIRST goal (like PostHog) is to land ONE proper trace to the platform in minutes, THEN reach full coverage.
0. FIRST-TRACE PATH (do this first, fast): pick the SIMPLEST high-value feature from the anchors — ideally a non-streaming request→LLM→response route. Add neatlogs.init() + the skill-selected wrapper/handler/hook/processor, then build and exercise that exact path yourself through verify_run so a proper rooted trace lands. A supported wrapper owns its LLM span; never add a second manual LLM trace. When the feature is multi-step, add a WORKFLOW span only to group the steps under one named root. Do NOT defer init()/the first feature to the end.
   RETRIEVAL-AND-GENERATION EXAMPLE: for a feature that retrieves stored context and then generates an answer, keep the app's existing retrieval and prompt construction unchanged. Instrument the user-facing route/command as WORKFLOW (only when it groups multiple steps), and use the framework/provider integration for the model call. If the selected wrapper/handler/hook/processor/instrumentor actually captures the retrieval operation, it owns that RETRIEVER span—never add a duplicate manual RETRIEVER span. Otherwise add a manual RETRIEVER for the custom/unsupported lookup, use neatlogs.retriever.* attributes only, and never generate neatlogs.retrieval.*. Expected shape: WORKFLOW → RETRIEVER + one integration-owned LLM. Build, restart the process that loads init, invoke the documented retrieval-and-generation path, and confirm that exact run in Neatlogs. Never add a manual LLM decorator beside the integration.
1. THEN fan out: dispatch the remaining per-file `instrumentor` subagents in parallel — put MULTIPLE Agent tool calls (8-16) in ONE assistant message so they run concurrently; do NOT send one Agent call, wait, then send the next (that serializes the whole phase and is the #1 cause of a slow run). Each subagent gets ONE file + its exact `file:line` anchors + function→kind list; tell them to Grep straight to those lines (no full-file read). Distinct files to distinct subagents. (Package install runs as a background task alongside.)
2. The global wiring (init/.env/wrap) is already done from step 0; just register any remaining framework handler/processor.
3. Keep each wave wide (≈8-16 concurrent). Prioritise RAW-HTTP LLM files and custom TOOL/RETRIEVER files not actually captured by the selected wrapper/handler/hook/processor/instrumentor.
4. VERIFY — proportional, not a blanket sweep (do these on the EDITED files only, using the subagent reports to know what changed):
   a. Compile-check ONLY the files that were edited (Python: `python -m py_compile <those files>`; TS: `tsc --noEmit` / `node --check`). When several files need FIXES, fan the fixes out the same way as step 1 — multiple `instrumentor` Agent calls in ONE message (each given the file + the precise problem to fix), NOT one fix at a time. Serial re-editing in this phase is what makes a run drag.
   b. ADVERSARIAL contract check on each `neatlogs.trace(...)`/`@neatlogs.span(...)` site ADDED (read just those sites — these are RUNTIME bugs a compile check passes over). Assume it is broken until you confirm each: (i) ARGS are valid for the call. A `@neatlogs.span(...)` decorator needs ONLY `kind=` — the span name DEFAULTS to the function name, so a bare `@neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW")` is correct and preferred; an explicit name is the OPTIONAL `name=` kwarg. `neatlogs.trace(...)` needs a name as its FIRST POSITIONAL (`trace("name", kind=...)`) and must not also pass `name=` (both → `TypeError: got multiple values for argument name`) nor omit it (`trace(kind=...)` → missing name). NEVER pass `workflow_name=` to `@span()`/`trace()` — that raises `TypeError: span() got an unexpected keyword argument workflow_name` and crashes at import; `workflow_name=` exists ONLY on `neatlogs.init()`. (ii) `.set_attribute(...)` is on the SPAN (the `as span:` / `__enter__()` return), never on the `trace()` context-manager value. (iii) manual streaming spans `__exit__` exactly once. (iv) NO DUPLICATE span on an already-instrumented call — if the call is an SDK client you `wrap()`ed (or a framework handler covers it), do NOT also wrap it in a manual `trace(kind="LLM")`; and do NOT nest a same-kind span inside another (e.g. `@span(kind="EMBEDDING")` on a fn whose body opens `trace(kind="EMBEDDING")`). One logical call = one span of that kind. (iv-b) EVERY `neatlogs.wrap(X)` you added: X MUST be a supported vendor SDK client (OpenAI/AsyncOpenAI, Anthropic/AsyncAnthropic, google.genai.Client, CrewAI Crew/Flow, Pydantic AI Agent, DSPy module, Agno agent, Google ADK Runner, Strands). If X is `httpx.AsyncClient(...)`, `requests.Session(...)`, `aiohttp.ClientSession(...)`, or a boto3 client, `wrap()` raises `TypeError` at IMPORT — REMOVE the wrap(), restore the bare construction, and put a MANUAL `trace()` span on the `.post()`/`.stream()` CALL instead (raw-http rule). This is a hard import-time crash, not a style nit — step 4a `py_compile` only PARSES (never imports), so it cannot catch it; you MUST verify it here. (v) any LLM/EMBEDDING/RERANKER span sets the OUTPUT (`neatlogs.llm.output` etc.), not just input. Fix any site that fails.
   c. Confirm no health/readiness/ping/warmup/startup function got a span (commandment F).
   d. Confirm each feature has exactly ONE WORKFLOW root (commandment B); streaming/SSE handlers open the WORKFLOW span INSIDE the generator (commandment G). You are blocked from stopping until WORKFLOW + raw-HTTP + tool categories are covered.
   e. Call mcp__wizard-tools__verify_run with a SAFE, documented representative command. For a server, pass its start command plus exercise_command so the tool restarts the rebuilt process and invokes the real user route. It injects the key and an ephemeral correlation marker only into that launched process, then the WIZARD (not you) polls the exact marker every 2 seconds for up to 10 minutes, waits for backend finalization, pages through every span, and verifies required application I/O. Never put credentials or invent a marker in tool input. Do not add your own polling loop or repeatedly call verify_run after a timeout unless you first exercise a new real application run.
   f. Treat a successful verify_run result as the final platform gate. The parent Wizard owns authenticated persisted-trace readback, waits for finalization, pages through every span, and verifies hierarchy plus required application I/O before returning success. Do not call hosted Neatlogs tools, search for another trace, poll processing yourself, invent a verification ID, or ask for a new verification tool.
   g. Inspect the persisted shape: one root, nested children, exactly one integration-owned LLM span per real call, no health-only traces, and requested session/end-user identity. Persisted WORKFLOW, AGENT, LLM, TOOL, and MCP_TOOL spans must have non-empty input_value AND output_value; event-like/infrastructure spans can legitimately be one-sided. A single missing required application input/output fails verification. Local span logs are diagnostic only.
   h. If a browser-only web path cannot be exercised with the available tools, do not pretend setup succeeded and do not ask the user to rerun setup. Give one UUID and the COMPLETE sequence: preserve existing OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES while adding `neatlogs.verification.marker=<uuid>`, restart the web app with that environment, exercise the real path in the browser, then run `npx @neatlogs/wizard verify --api-key <key> --verification-marker <same-uuid> --expected-root-span <the exact root span name>`. The marker and expected root are mandatory. Verify is read-only: it never detects, edits, builds, installs, or invokes the coding agent.

### Model call sites (1) — each needs a span, but CLASSIFY BY THE MODEL'S JOB (the analyzer can't tell these apart — that's your call):
Do NOT blindly use kind="LLM". Pick the specific kind: an EMBEDDING model (text→vector: titan-embed, .embeddings.create, embed_documents, invoke_model on an *embed* model) → kind="EMBEDDING"; a RERANK model (query+docs→scores: cohere.rerank, invoke_model on a *rerank* model) → kind="RERANKER"; a generate/chat/completion model → kind="LLM". Apply per callStyle:
- **framework** — framework → use its installed-skill mechanism (callback handler, hook, processor, runner wrapper, or native telemetry); add no manual LLM trace around covered calls:
    - lib\agent\smoke-graph.ts:31  callModel

### Independent workflows (10 candidate roots) — ONE WORKFLOW span per genuine feature, do NOT merge
Each entry below is an INDEPENDENT feature = its OWN trace root. Open exactly ONE WORKFLOW span per genuine feature; every CHAIN/AGENT/TOOL/RETRIEVER/LLM span it reaches nests UNDER that one WORKFLOW. A different feature is a SEPARATE sibling root — never nest one WORKFLOW inside another, never merge two features into one. The `evidence` is the raw structural signal (verbatim decorator / shape) — YOU decide the kind (HTTP route, CLI command, cron, queue/stream consumer, event handler, library API, agent loop). A WORKFLOW DECORATOR needs only `kind` — `@neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW")` (the name defaults to the function name; an explicit name is the OPTIONAL `name=`). NEVER pass `workflow_name=` to @span()/trace() (that kwarg exists only on neatlogs.init() — on a span it crashes at import). SKIP candidates that are health/readiness/ping/warmup/boot or internal helpers (commandment F). For a multiplexed entry (one handler dispatching on task type / msg.topic), open the WORKFLOW span PER BRANCH with a per-feature name — every independently-running workflow gets its own trace.

5	## 1. `init()` in `instrumentation.ts` via the `register()` hook — use a DYNAMIC import (REQUIRED)
6	
7	Next.js runs `register()` once at server startup — the right place for `init()`. Your route handlers then create a `langchainHandler()` and pass it via `{ callbacks: [handler] }`; LangChain imports in those routes can be plain static imports.

13	export async function register() {
14	  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === "nodejs") {
15	    const { init, flush, shutdown } = await import("neatlogs"); // dynamic, not top-level

17	    await init({

29	  mask?: MaskFunction;      // Per-span mask function
30	  internal?: boolean;       // Mark as internal span
31	
32	  // Agent-specific
33	  role?: string;            // AGENT: agent role
34	  goal?: string;            // AGENT: agent goal
35	
36	  // Tool-specific
37	  toolName?: string;        // TOOL/MCP_TOOL: tool name
38	  parameters?: Record<string, any>;  // TOOL: tool parameters
39	  toolJsonSchema?: Record<string, any>;  // MCP_TOOL: JSON schema
40	
41	  // Embedding-specific
42	  model?: string;           // EMBEDDING: model name
43	  dimension?: number;       // EMBEDDING: embedding dimension
44	}
45	```
46	
47	> **Note**: Unlike the Python SDK, the TypeScript `SpanOptions` does NOT have `captureStdout`, `tags`, or `version` fields.
48	
49	### Valid Kinds
50	
51	`span()` throws an `Error` for any kind not in this set:
52	
53	`WORKFLOW`, `AGENT`, `CHAIN`, `TOOL`, `RETRIEVER`, `EMBEDDING`, `GUARDRAIL`, `MCP_TOOL`
54	
55	### When to Use Each Kind
56	
57	#### WORKFLOW
58	
59	Top-level entry point that orchestrates the full pipeline.
60	
61	```typescript
62	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
63	
64	const runPipeline = span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async (topic: string) => {
65	  const analysis = await researcher(topic);
66	  const report = await writer(analysis);
67	  return report;
68	});
69	```
70	
71	#### AGENT
72	
73	Function representing an AI agent with a specific role/goal.
74	
75	```typescript
76	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
77	
78	const researcher = span(
79	  { kind: 'AGENT', name: 'researcher', role: 'Research Analyst', goal: 'Find relevant information' },
80	  async (topic: string) => {
81	    // ... agent logic with LLM calls ...
82	    return findings;
83	  },
84	);
85	```
86	
87	#### CHAIN
88	
89	Sequential processing step for intermediate processing or pipeline stages.
90	
91	```typescript
92	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
93	
94	const processDocuments = span({ kind: 'CHAIN' }, async (docs: string[]) => {
95	  return docs.map((d) => d.trim().toLowerCase());
96	});
97	```
98	
99	#### TOOL
100	
101	Tool/function call (web search, calculator, API call, etc.).
102	
103	```typescript
104	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
105	
106	const webSearch = span(
107	  { kind: 'TOOL', toolName: 'web_search', description: 'Search the web' },
108	  async (query: string) => {
109	    return await searchApi.search(query);
110	  },
111	);
112	```
113	
114	#### RETRIEVER
115	
116	RAG retrieval. Automatically extracts documents from the return value.
117	
118	```typescript
119	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
120	
121	const retrieveDocs = span({ kind: 'RETRIEVER' }, async (query: string) => {
122	  return await vectorDb.search(query, { topK: 5 });
123	});
124	```
125	
126	The RETRIEVER postprocessor automatically:
127	- Extracts the query from function args named `query`, `question`, or `text`
128	- Extracts documents from array results or objects with `documents`/`docs`/`results` keys
129	- Sets canonical `neatlogs.retriever.documents.N.{content,id,score,metadata}` attributes for every returned document; do not truncate results client-side
130	
131	#### EMBEDDING
132	
133	Embedding generation.
134	
135	```typescript
136	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
137	
138	const embedTexts = span(
139	  { kind: 'EMBEDDING', model: 'text-embedding-3-small', dimension: 1536 },
140	  async (texts: string[]) => {
141	    return await embeddingModel.encode(texts);
142	  },
143	);
144	```
145	
146	#### GUARDRAIL
147	
148	Input/output validation and safety checks.
149	
150	```typescript
151	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
152	
153	const checkToxicity = span({ kind: 'GUARDRAIL' }, async (text: string) => {
154	  const result = await toxicityModel.check(text);
155	  return { passed: result.score < 0.5, score: result.score };
156	});
157	```
158	
159	#### MCP_TOOL
160	
161	MCP protocol tool handlers. Automatically wraps string results as `{ result: "..." }` and extracts input from the first argument.
162	
163	```typescript
164	import { span } from 'neatlogs';
165	
166	const getWeather = span(
167	  { kind: 'MCP_TOOL', toolName: 'get_weather', description: 'Get current weather' },
168	  async (location: string) => {
169	    return `Weather in ${location}: Sunny, 72°F`;
170	  },
171	);
172	```
173	
174	### `captureInput` / `captureOutput`
175	
176	Default is `true` for both. Set to `false` to suppress serialization — useful for large payloads or sensitive data.
177	
178	```typescript
179	const processLargeFile = span(
180	  { kind: 'CHAIN', captureInput: false, captureOutput: false },
181	  async (data: Buffer) => { /* ... */ },
182	);
183	```
184	
185	### Complete Multi-Agent Example
186	
187	```typescript
188	import { init, wrapOpenAI, span, flush, shutdown } from 'neatlogs';
189	import { OpenAI } from 'openai';
190	
191	await init({
192	  apiKey: '...',
193	  workflowName: 'research-app',
194	});
195	
196	const client = wrapOpenAI(new OpenAI());
197	
198	const webSearch = span(
199	  { kind: 'TOOL', toolName: 'web_search' },
200	  async (query: string) => {
201	    return `Results for: ${query}`;
202	  },
203	);
204	
205	const researcher = span(
206	  { kind: 'AGENT', name: 'researcher', role: 'Research Analyst' },
207	  async (topic: string) => {
208	    const searchResults = await webSearch(topic);
209	    const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
210	      model: 'gpt-4o',

214	  },
215	);
216	
217	const runPipeline = span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async (topic: string) => {
218	  return await researcher(topic);
219	});
220	
221	await runPipeline('quantum computing');
222	await flush();
223	await shutdown();
224	```

252	
253	## 3. `trace()` Callback Wrapper
254	
255	For unsupported/custom operations that need direct canonical span attributes.
256	Do not use `trace()` as a second LLM capture layer around a call
257	owned by a wrapper, handler, hook, processor, or instrumentor.
258	
259	### Signature
260	
261	```typescript
262	import { trace } from 'neatlogs';
263	import type { TraceOptions } from 'neatlogs';
264	
265	const result = await trace(options: TraceOptions, async (span) => {
266	  // user code runs here with the span active
267	  return value;
268	});
269	```
270	
271	### TraceOptions
272	
273	```typescript
274	interface TraceOptions {
275	  name: string;                  // Required: span name
276	  kind?: SpanKind;               // Span kind (default: 'CHAIN')
277	  mask?: MaskFunction;           // Per-trace mask function
278	  attributes?: Record<string, any>;  // Custom span attributes
279	}
280	```
281	
282	**IMPORTANT**: Unlike `span()`, `trace()` does NOT validate the kind string at runtime. It accepts extended values including `'LLM'`, `'RERANKER'`, and `'VECTOR_STORE'`, although the current `TraceOptions.kind` type is narrower; use `kind: 'LLM' as any` (or the corresponding extended kind) at that boundary. Use `'LLM'` only when this manual trace is the sole capture owner for an unsupported/raw call.
283	
284	When `kind` is not provided, it defaults to `'CHAIN'`.
285	
286	### Sessions & end-user
287	
288	Session and end-user identity are **per-request** and set at the **trace root** — never on `init()` (`init()` does NOT take `sessionId` / `autoSession`).
289	
290	Per turn, set them on the root `trace()` or `span()`:
291	
292	```typescript
293	await trace(
294	  { name: 'turn', sessionId: 'conv_123', endUserId: 'u_456', endUserMetadata: { plan: 'pro' } },
295	  async () => { /* this turn's work */ },
296	);
297	
298	// or on a root span:
299	await span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW', sessionId: 'conv_123', endUserId: 'u_456' }, fn)();
300	```
301	
302	Wrapper-only code (only `wrap(...)` calls, no manual root) uses `identify()` — the wrapper's auto-root inherits it:
303	
304	```typescript
305	await identify({ sessionId: 'conv_123', endUserId: 'u_456' }, async () => {
306	  /* wrapped LLM call */
307	});
308	```
309	
310	Reuse the same `sessionId` on every turn to group them into one session; the end-user is per session. Identity is **root-only** — set it once on the root and the backend rolls it up across the trace.
311	
312	### Span Object Methods
313	
314	The `span` parameter in the callback is an OpenTelemetry `Span`. Available methods:
315	
316	```typescript
317	await trace({ name: 'my_op', kind: 'CHAIN' }, async (span) => {
318	  span.setAttribute('key', 'value');        // Add a custom attribute
319	  span.recordException(error);               // Record an exception
320	  span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR, message: 'msg' });
321	  span.addEvent('event_name', { key: 'val' });
322	});
323	```
324	
325	### Use Cases for `trace()`
326	
327	1. **Custom attribute capture** — use `span.setAttribute()` inside the callback
328	2. **Unsupported/raw operations** — create a manual span only when no wrapper, callback, hook, processor, native telemetry, or provider instrumentor owns it
329	3. **Span kinds not available in `span()`**: `'LLM'`, `'RERANKER'`, `'VECTOR_STORE'`
330	
331	### Common Anti-Pattern
332	
333	Do NOT wrap a function that already uses `span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' })` in `trace()` — it's redundant:
334	
335	```typescript
336	// ❌ WRONG: Redundant wrapper
337	const myWorkflow = span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async () => { /* ... */ });
338	await trace({ name: 'main' }, async () => {
339	  await myWorkflow();  // Already traced by span()
340	});
341	
342	// ✅ CORRECT: Just call it directly
343	await myWorkflow();
344	```

348	## 4. `log()` — Structured Logging
349	
350	Capture timestamped log steps within the current trace.
351	
352	### Signature
353	
354	```typescript
355	import { log } from 'neatlogs';
356	
357	log(msgTemplate: string, options?: Record<string, any>);
358	```
359	
360	### Usage
361	
362	```typescript
363	import { log } from 'neatlogs';
364	
365	log('Processing query: {query}', { query: 'What is TypeScript?', level: 'info' });
366	log('Retrieved {count} documents', { count: 5 });
367	```
368	
369	- `msgTemplate` uses `{key}` placeholders (single braces)
370	- `options` provides template variables and an optional `level` (default: `'info'`)
371	- Requires `captureLogs: true` in `init()` for OTel LogRecord emission
372	- In debug mode, logs are echoed to console

376	## 5. Combine orchestration with automatically captured calls
377	
378	Use `span()` to represent real custom orchestration. Call handler-owned operations directly inside it; do not add an LLM `trace()` around them. Use a manual LLM trace only for an unsupported/raw call outside LangChain.
379	
380	## 6. Custom Span Attributes via `trace()`
381	
382	`LLM` is root-eligible. Current manual APIs add one `WORKFLOW` parent when another semantic kind would otherwise be parentless; nested calls keep their real parent. The LangChain handler also self-roots its supported runs.
383	
384	Manual spans must use these exact canonical keys:
385	
386	| Kind | Exact canonical attributes |
387	|---|---|
388	| `LLM` | Required when available: `neatlogs.llm.provider`, `neatlogs.llm.model_name`, `neatlogs.llm.input_messages.{i}.role`, `neatlogs.llm.input_messages.{i}.content`, `neatlogs.llm.output_messages.{i}.role`, `neatlogs.llm.output_messages.{i}.content`, `neatlogs.llm.token_count.prompt`, `neatlogs.llm.token_count.completion`, `neatlogs.llm.token_count.total`. Also report `neatlogs.llm.system`, `neatlogs.llm.finish_reason` or `neatlogs.llm.stop_reason`, `neatlogs.llm.is_streaming`, `neatlogs.llm.temperature`, `neatlogs.llm.top_p`, `neatlogs.llm.top_k`, `neatlogs.llm.max_tokens`, and `neatlogs.llm.invocation_parameters` when known. |
389	| `RETRIEVER` | `neatlogs.retriever.query`, `neatlogs.retriever.top_k`, `neatlogs.retriever.documents.{i}`, `neatlogs.retriever.input`, `neatlogs.retriever.output` |
390	| `RERANKER` | `neatlogs.reranker.model_name`, `neatlogs.reranker.query`, `neatlogs.reranker.top_k`, `neatlogs.reranker.input_documents.{i}`, `neatlogs.reranker.output_documents.{i}`, `neatlogs.reranker.input`, `neatlogs.reranker.output` |
391	| `VECTOR_STORE` | `neatlogs.db.system`, `neatlogs.db.operation`, `neatlogs.db.collection_name`, `neatlogs.vectordb.index_name`, `neatlogs.vectordb.embedding_model`, `neatlogs.vectordb.vector_dimension`, `neatlogs.vectordb.similarity_algorithm`, `neatlogs.vector_store.input`, `neatlogs.vector_store.output` |
392	| `EMBEDDING` | `neatlogs.embedding.model_name`, `neatlogs.embedding.text`, `neatlogs.embedding.token_count`, `neatlogs.embedding.vector`, `neatlogs.embedding.invocation_parameters`, `neatlogs.embedding.input`, `neatlogs.embedding.output` |
393	| `GUARDRAIL` | `neatlogs.guardrail.input`, `neatlogs.guardrail.output`, `neatlogs.guardrail.passed`, `neatlogs.guardrail.score` |
394	| `EVALUATOR` | `neatlogs.evaluator.input`, `neatlogs.evaluator.output`; encode evaluator name, criteria, and score in JSON `neatlogs.metadata` until dedicated evaluator fields exist |
395	
396	Use indexed document keys. Do not emit the legacy `neatlogs.retrieval.*` namespace or invented keys such as `neatlogs.vector_store.query`.
397	
398	### RERANKER
399	
400	```typescript
401	import { trace } from 'neatlogs';
402	
403	async function rerank(query: string, docs: string[], topN = 3) {
404	  return await trace({ name: 'rerank', kind: 'RERANKER' as any }, async (span) => {
405	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.reranker.query', query);
406	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.reranker.top_k', topN);
407	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.reranker.model_name', 'cohere-rerank-v3');
408	    docs.forEach((doc, i) =>
409	      span.setAttribute(`neatlogs.reranker.input_documents.${i}`, JSON.stringify(doc)),
410	    );
411	    const reranked = await rerankerModel.rerank(query, docs, topN);
412	    reranked.forEach((doc, i) =>
413	      span.setAttribute(`neatlogs.reranker.output_documents.${i}`, JSON.stringify(doc)),
414	    );
415	    return reranked;
416	  });
417	}
418	```
419	
420	### VECTOR_STORE
421	
422	```typescript
423	import { trace } from 'neatlogs';
424	
425	async function upsertDocuments(indexName: string, docs: Document[]) {
426	  return await trace({ name: 'upsert_documents', kind: 'VECTOR_STORE' as any }, async (span) => {
427	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.db.system', 'custom_vector_db');
428	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.db.operation', 'upsert');
429	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.vectordb.index_name', indexName);
430	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.vector_store.input', JSON.stringify(docs));
431	    const result = await vectorDb.upsert(indexName, docs);
432	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.vector_store.output', JSON.stringify(result));
433	    return result;
434	  });
435	}
436	```
437	
438	Use `RETRIEVER` for vector search/query. `VECTOR_STORE` is for writes and index-management operations.

440	### Manual LLM Span (No SDK to Patch)
441	
442	When calling an LLM API directly without an instrumented SDK:
443	
444	```typescript
445	import { trace } from 'neatlogs';
446	
447	async function rawLlmCall(prompt: string) {
448	  return await trace({ name: 'raw_api_request', kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async () =>
449	    trace({ name: 'raw_api_llm_call', kind: 'LLM' as any }, async (span) => {
450	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.internal', false);
451	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.provider', 'openai');
452	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.model_name', 'gpt-4o');
453	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.input_messages.0.role', 'user');
454	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.input_messages.0.content', prompt);
455	
456	    const response = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', {
457	      method: 'POST',
458	      headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
459	      body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-4o', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }] }),
460	    });
461	    if (!response.ok) throw new Error('LLM request failed: ' + response.status);
462	    const data = await response.json();
463	
464	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.output_messages.0.role', 'assistant');
465	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.output_messages.0.content', data.choices?.[0]?.message?.content ?? '');
466	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.token_count.prompt', data.usage.prompt_tokens);
467	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.token_count.completion', data.usage.completion_tokens);
468	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.token_count.total', data.usage.total_tokens);
469	    span.setAttribute('neatlogs.llm.finish_reason', data.choices?.[0]?.finish_reason ?? '');
470	    return data;
471	    }),
472	  );
473	}
474	```
475
